yarn.meaning: All details kept: November 13, 2025 start, Recreation.gov and offices, the Walatowa Saturdays 9-4 from November 22 to December 20, 2024, pre-cut trees and priority, $10 non-refundable, $2.50 fee, 5 inch/10 foot tag rule, 15-foot example, Every Kid Outdoors, forest-health rationale.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "Give us a bell for current opening hours", "get first dibs", "patches where heaps of skinny little trees are all crammed in", "where the wildlife can find a feed". "good for the bush" fits forest health in Aussie usage.
yarn.authenticity: Sounds like a friendly Aussie notice: "Good news if you're after a real Chrissie tree", "Just pop in the pass or voucher number", "heads up".
yarn.register: A level-2 touch: everyday Aussie words in a plain notice; no swearing.
yarn.tone: Stays an informative notice, though "Good news" and "here's a bonus" make it a bit more promotional than the neutral original.
yarn.flow: Reads smoothly, with the original's order intact.
yarn.variety: Varied: "Chrissie", "have a good read", "give us a bell", "first dibs", "pop in", "heads up", "the bush", "find a feed".

unharnessed.meaning: Every fact kept, closely following the original.
unharnessed.sense: "up for grabs", "first dibs", "skinny trees", "Get in touch with us" all fit.
unharnessed.authenticity: Plain, natural Australian English; nothing forced.
unharnessed.register: On the light side of level 2: only "up for grabs" and "first dibs" stand out; otherwise a plain-English rewrite.
unharnessed.variety: Very few Aussie terms to vary; little to lean on but little there.

engine.meaning: Text is the original almost verbatim, so the facts survive.
engine.sense: "Local bush health experts" turns forest-health specialists into something odd, and "improves bush health" strains; "Chrissie tree permits" is fine.
engine.authenticity: Two word-swaps ("Chrissie", "bush") dropped into untouched agency prose ("Availability is subject to weather conditions and supply"); mixes "Chrissie tree" and "Christmas Tree" inconsistently.
engine.flow: Reads as the original; the "Chrissie"/"Christmas" switching is a little jarring.

summaries.yarn: A natural, complete level-2 notice with well-chosen everyday Aussie; slightly chirpier than the original.
summaries.unharnessed: A clean, faithful plain-English rewrite with a couple of Aussie touches, a little light for the brief.
summaries.engine: The original with "Chrissie" and "bush" swapped in; barely translated and one awkward swap.
